concepts: you-ball-goal: my body is behind the ball (ball x > my x in my attack frame). strategy.md "Frame".
Body within half a pole (3 m) of the ball along x: where farm1 "gets bad" and the tip starts to decide the side (strategy.md round 2 + round 3).

Near the ball with the pole tip behind it (tip x < ball x): hooked to PUSH the ball on, good even with the body slightly past (strategy.md round 3; the user's "0-89 deg" was stated attacking left, i.e. back-up in the attack frame — see the data note there).
Near the ball with the tip beyond it (tip x >= ball x): can only pull the ball back = effectively the dreaded situation (strategy.md round 3).
Good side with room: more than half a pole behind the ball — can vault straight into it.
Good side but within half a pole of the ball: time to back up (strategy.md round 2).
Situation A, you-opp-ball: past the ball with the opponent between me and it, on his good side.
Situation B, opp-you-ball ("you're fucked"): past the ball, between it and the opponent.
Both riders past the ball (from my side's view).
Kill window: I'm in play, the opponent is not (killed and waiting 3 s to respawn, or his 0.3 s spawn ghost). "Kill: very often guarantees a goal" (strategy.md round 2).
The opponent is past the ball from his point of view (he attacks -x: ball x > his x) — what tip peeking and the throw aim for ("GG").
Feet off everything (the game's foot sensor: not on the ground or on a pole). Riders pogo on the pole, so this is true most of the time (farm2 ~72%).
Pole tip on the floor (tip less than PLANTED_H = 0.35 m above it): the slingshot is loading.
Body in a pit (|x| > 16.3 m and below plateau level, as h2h_breakdown.py).
Pole quadrant -90..0 deg (attack frame): forward and down — the normal low carry / planting.
Pole quadrant 0..90 deg: forward and up.
Pole quadrant 90..180 deg: back and up (near the ball: the hooked-to-push pole).
Pole quadrant 180..270 deg: back and down.
Airborne, tip off the floor, pole rotating backward (counter-clockwise in the attack frame, > 1 rad/s): the user's trick that prolongs a jump and fine-tunes its height (strategy.md "Normal play").
My pole (outer 80%, straight body->tip line) within 1 m of the opponent's body centre: contact / pressing proxy (strategy.md situation B "keep your pole on him").
The opponent's pole within 1 m of my body: he presses me (situation B "the opponent presses you down").

My pole passes over the opponent: at his x (between 25% and 105% of my pole's length out) the pole line is 0.6-2.5 m above his body centre. Situation A option 2: "put your pole over his head: threatens a kill and limits his movement" (kills are stomps: the upper rider wins).

The opponent stands on my pole: his foot sensor is down (on_ground), he is more than 1 m above the floor, his body is within 1.5 m of my pole line and above it. The setup of the throw (strategy.md "From above — the throw"). (On_ground at height is ~90% someone's pole: checked against full snapshots.)
I stand on the opponent's pole (mirror of opp_on_my_pole): he can throw me.

Tip peeking: the opponent and I are on opposite sides of the ball and my tip is past the ball on his side, between the ball and him and at most half a pole past the ball — the order "opp-(our tip)-ball-us" (strategy.md "Ball handling").

Situation B defence: in B now, my pole on the opponent in >= half of the last 2 s, and my pole's rotation reversed >= 4 times in them (|w| > 0.5 rad/s; >= 1 Hz push/pull; the user eyeballed 2-3 Hz) — "alternate pressing and releasing" (strategy.md situation B + round 2 timing).
My side scored (my score went up).

I killed the opponent: he drops out of play with the 3 s death timer (respawn_in > 0.5). In 1v1 only rider contacts set it (deleter falls and post-goal respawns give <= 0.1); matches the game's kill stats 186/186 in farm2 self-play. "Kill: very often guarantees a goal".
I was killed (my 3 s death timer started).

Backward swing over the top: the pole passes vertical going backward (angle crosses 90 deg upward, counter-clockwise in the attack frame), as analysis/pole_rotation.py. The rotation all agents struggle with (HANDOFF farm3).
Forward swing over the top (angle crosses 90 deg downward): every normal vault stride does one.

A slingshot launch: the tip leaves the floor after a planted phase (>= 2 steps) in which the body rose at >= 6 m/s, and the body is airborne at release (strategy.md "Vaulting = a slingshot"). Marked at the release; length = the planted phase. (farm2 vaults reach 10-15 m/s.)

Landing on the pole to store energy: a vault (see `vault`) whose planted phase began while airborne and falling at >= 3 m/s and in which the body never touched down — the fall was caught by the pole and turned into the next jump (strategy.md "Landing: store kinetic + gravitational energy ... -> bigger next jump"). The robust proxy we have: the pole's bend is not in the observation.

Situation A option 1, the long jump over the ball: I was in A within the last 2 s, and now, airborne and moving backward (vx < -1 m/s, so I moved, not the ball), I cross to the good side and stay there for 0.5 s. Marked when confirmed (crossing + 0.5 s); length from the last A moment.

I pushed the opponent to the wrong side: he had been on his good side for >= 0.5 s, crosses past the ball (from his view) while my pole touched him or he stood on it in the last 1 s, and stays wrong (or dies) for 1 s. "makes him miss and land on the wrong side ... GG" (strategy.md "Ball handling"). Marked when confirmed; length from the first contact step considered.
Near the ball my tip went from past the ball to behind it and stays 0.33 s: re-hooked to push (strategy.md round 3; also the goal of the B defence for the opponent's tip). Marked when confirmed.

The throw: the opponent stood on my pole for >= 0.2 s, and within 0.5 s of leaving it he flies, airborne, at >= 8 m/s and >= 4 m/s faster than while on it (I flung him; riders also just bounce off a pole) — strategy.md "From above — the throw: when the opponent steps on our pole we fling it and he flies". Marked at the first step the launch speed is reached; length from when he left the pole.

Tip peeking from below pays off: while peeking (my tip between the ball and the opponent), my tip touches him (tip within 1 m of his body) as he is airborne going at the ball — "a slight touch on the opponent as he vaults at the ball makes him miss" (strategy.md "Ball handling"). Marked at the touch.
